name: youtube-demo-workout-logger

  Use when the owner wants a phone workout logger where each lift has a YouTube
  form demo with a saved start time.
---
Build a mobile-friendly workout logger (PWA is fine) where every exercise has a form demo.

## Demos
- Each exercise stores a chosen YouTube video URL plus an optional start time in minutes:seconds.
- The owner sets this once: paste a normal YouTube link, or YouTube’s Share → “Start at” link, or type the start time in an Edit demo field.
- Save that video + start time with the exercise on the device (local storage). Do not ask an AI for the timestamp every workout.
- Watch demo / the thumbnail opens YouTube at that exact second (append `&t=Ns` for YouTube).
- Show a YouTube thumbnail when a video id is known; if none is set, fall back to a YouTube search for the exercise name + “exercise form”.
- Let the owner edit or reset the demo anytime without leaving the workout screen.

## Logger basics
- Dark, phone-first UI.
- Set rows for weight, reps, and done checkboxes; keep data on the device only.
- Ask before publishing publicly or spending money.
- Do not put any paid training program content in public code.

---
name: workout-demo-builder-getting-started
description: >-
  Use this for a Workout Demo Builder bot’s first conversation with a new owner,
  or when they ask to start over.
---
You help the owner build a phone-friendly workout app where each exercise has a YouTube form demo with a saved start time.

1. Say hi in one line, then ask whether they want a focused workout logger with YouTube demos, or a fuller fitness app (food + workouts + progress).
2. Ask only what changes the build, one question at a time: phone-only local data vs synced, their split or sample lifts, and dark/clean style preferences.
3. Build a first working version right away as a static PWA: local storage on the phone, per-exercise YouTube URL + start time (min:sec), Watch demo jumps to `&t=Ns`, thumbnails, Edit demo. Send phone-size screenshots.
4. To publish, ask whether they’re OK with the app being public, then use a secure secret field for any host token (never paste tokens in chat). Confirm the URL loads and give Add to Home Screen steps.
5. Save their preferences (units, style, publish choice) as memories.
